ALS Machine Learning Exploration

Predicting forest inventory attributes from airborne laser scanning metrics

Jessica Middleton

2026-06-12

1 Introduction

Source repository: https://github.com/SkudnikM/flai-tree-stats-lidar

Goal: predict forest inventory attributes per plot from airborne laser scanning (ALS/lidar) metrics.

Data

  • ALS-NGI_plot_param.csv: lidar-derived plot metrics (the predictors).
  • poploskvah.csv: field-measured inventory values (the targets).

Targets modelled: Nha (stems per hectare), Gha (basal area per hectare, m²/ha) and Vol_1v_ha (volume per hectare, m³/ha).

Workflow (identical for every target)

  1. Read and join the two tables, then clean NA values.
  2. Explore the data and apply a Yeo-Johnson transformation to skewed predictors.
  3. Split the data 80/20 into a training set and a holdout test set.
  4. Compare 5 models with 5-fold cross-validation (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Elastic Net, SVM Radial, KNN).
  5. Tune the best model and compare it with its untuned (baseline) version.
  6. Evaluate the tuned model once on the untouched holdout set.

Notes on method

  • Only lidar metrics are used as predictors. The other inventory columns (NhaRob, G, GhaRob, Vol_1v, Vol_1v_haRob, agb) are excluded to avoid data leakage.
  • Targets stay on their original scale, so RMSE is in the units of the data.
  • Centring and scaling happen inside each cross-validation fold (caret preProcess).

2 Setup

2.1 Packages

packages <- c("tidyverse", "moments", "bestNormalize", "patchwork", "ggridges",
              "caret", "randomForest", "gbm", "glmnet", "kernlab", "knitr")

# Install any package that is missing, then load all of them
for (pkg in packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
  library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}

2.2 Plot style

All figures share one theme and one colour palette, so the report looks consistent.

# Forest-inspired colours
forest_dark  <- "#1B4332"
forest_mid   <- "#2D6A4F"
forest_light <- "#B7E4C7"
accent       <- "#E07A5F"   # used for "before", "baseline" and reference lines
paper        <- "#FBFBF8"   # plot background

# One fixed colour per model, used in every plot
model_cols <- c(Random_Forest     = "#2D6A4F",
                Gradient_Boosting = "#E07A5F",
                Elastic_Net       = "#3D5A80",
                SVM_Radial        = "#9C6ADE",
                KNN               = "#E9B44C")

theme_forest <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.3), colour = forest_dark),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption       = element_text(colour = "grey50", size = rel(0.8)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.background    = element_rect(fill = paper, colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major   = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.3),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", colour = forest_dark, hjust = 0),
      axis.title         = element_text(colour = "grey30"),
      legend.position    = "bottom"
    )
}
theme_set(theme_forest())

# Theme for the title area of combined (patchwork) figures
patch_theme <- theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = paper, colour = NA),
                     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, colour = forest_dark),
                     plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35"))

# "Random_Forest" -> "Random Forest"
pretty_name <- function(x) gsub("_", " ", x)

2.3 Small helper functions

rmse <- function(obs, pred) sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2))
r2   <- function(obs, pred) cor(obs, pred)^2

3 Data

3.1 Read data

plot_param <- read.csv("ALS-NGI_plot_param.csv")   # lidar metrics (predictors)
poploskvah <- read.csv("poploskvah.csv")           # field inventory (targets)

cat("plot_param:", nrow(plot_param), "rows,", ncol(plot_param), "columns\n")
## plot_param: 1000 rows, 97 columns
cat("poploskvah:", nrow(poploskvah), "rows,", ncol(poploskvah), "columns\n")
## poploskvah: 1000 rows, 12 columns

3.2 Join tables

poploskvah identifies a plot by plID and plLeto (year); plot_param uses plUID. A shared key plotNumber-year is built for both tables.

plot_param$substr_plUID <- str_sub(plot_param$plUID, end = -3)
poploskvah$substr_plUID <- paste(poploskvah$plID, poploskvah$plLeto, sep = "-")

full_df <- left_join(poploskvah, plot_param, by = "substr_plUID")

# Join quality checks
n_matched <- sum(poploskvah$substr_plUID %in% plot_param$substr_plUID)
cat("Plots with a lidar match:", n_matched, "of", nrow(poploskvah), "\n")
## Plots with a lidar match: 998 of 1000
cat("Duplicate keys in plot_param:", sum(duplicated(plot_param$substr_plUID)), "\n")
## Duplicate keys in plot_param: 1
cat("Rows before / after join:", nrow(poploskvah), "/", nrow(full_df), "\n")
## Rows before / after join: 1000 / 1000

5.2 Which lidar metrics are related to the targets?

Spearman correlation between every predictor and every target. Only the 20 predictors with the strongest average correlation are shown.

cor_df <- data.frame()
for (t in modeling_targets) {
  for (p in predictor_cols) {
    if (sd(cleaned_df[[p]]) > 0) {
      rho <- cor(cleaned_df[[p]], cleaned_df[[t]], method = "spearman")
      cor_df <- rbind(cor_df, data.frame(Target = t, Predictor = p, Rho = rho))
    }
  }
}

top_predictors <- cor_df %>%
  group_by(Predictor) %>%
  summarise(Mean_abs_rho = mean(abs(Rho))) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean_abs_rho)) %>%
  head(20)

cor_df %>%
  filter(Predictor %in% top_predictors$Predictor) %>%
  mutate(Predictor = factor(Predictor, levels = rev(top_predictors$Predictor))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Target, y = Predictor, fill = Rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = paper, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Rho), colour = abs(Rho) > 0.5),
            size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B5523B", mid = "#F7F5EE", high = forest_dark,
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman ρ") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "Lidar metrics most related to the targets",
       subtitle = "Top 20 predictors by mean |ρ| across the three targets",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))

6 Normalisation of Skewed Predictors

Predictors with |skewness| > 1 get a Yeo-Johnson transformation. Every decision is saved in transformation_log.

prepared_df <- cleaned_df
transformation_log <- data.frame()

for (col in predictor_cols) {
  x <- cleaned_df[[col]]

  if (sd(x) == 0) {
    # Constant column: nothing to transform
    method <- "Skipped (constant)"
    lambda <- NA
    skew_before <- NA
    skew_after <- NA
  } else {
    skew_before <- skewness(x)
    method <- "None"
    lambda <- NA
    skew_after <- skew_before

    if (abs(skew_before) > 1) {
      yj <- yeojohnson(x)
      prepared_df[[col]] <- predict(yj)
      method <- "Yeo-Johnson"
      lambda <- yj$lambda
      skew_after <- skewness(prepared_df[[col]])
    }
  }

  transformation_log <- rbind(transformation_log, data.frame(
    Variable = col, Transformation = method, Lambda = lambda,
    Original_Skewness = skew_before, Final_Skewness = skew_after))
}

kable(count(transformation_log, Transformation),
      caption = "Number of predictors per transformation outcome")
Number of predictors per transformation outcome
Transformation n
None 55
Skipped (constant) 3
Yeo-Johnson 28

6.1 Skewness before and after

transformed <- transformation_log %>%
  filter(Transformation == "Yeo-Johnson") %>%
  arrange(Original_Skewness) %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable))

ggplot(transformed, aes(y = Variable)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -1, xmax = 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = forest_light, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = Original_Skewness, xend = Final_Skewness, yend = Variable),
               colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = Original_Skewness), colour = accent, size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = Final_Skewness), colour = forest_dark, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Yeo-Johnson pulls skewed predictors back towards symmetry",
       subtitle = "Orange = before, green = after. Shaded band = |skewness| < 1",
       x = "Skewness", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))

6.2 Distributions before and after (ridgeline plot)

Every predictor is converted to z-scores so they can share one axis. Predictors are ordered by their original skewness.

to_long_z <- function(df, stage) {
  df %>%
    select(all_of(predictor_cols)) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Z") %>%
    mutate(Stage = stage)
}

skew_order <- transformation_log %>%
  filter(!is.na(Original_Skewness)) %>%
  arrange(Original_Skewness) %>%
  pull(Variable)

ridge_data <- bind_rows(to_long_z(cleaned_df, "Before transformation"),
                        to_long_z(prepared_df, "After transformation")) %>%
  filter(Variable %in% skew_order, is.finite(Z)) %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = skew_order),
         Stage = factor(Stage, levels = c("Before transformation", "After transformation")))

ggplot(ridge_data, aes(x = Z, y = Variable, fill = after_stat(x))) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(scale = 1.8, rel_min_height = 0.01,
                               colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "G", direction = -1, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Stage) +
  labs(title = "Every lidar metric, before and after normalisation",
       subtitle = "Z-scored densities; most skewed predictors at the top",
       x = "Z-score", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

7 Modelling Framework

Every target goes through exactly the same steps in run_target():

  1. Split: 80% training / 20% holdout test (seed 42).
  2. Benchmark: 5 models with the same 5 CV folds. Pre-processing (zv, nzv, centring, scaling) is done inside each fold.
  3. Select: the model with the lowest mean CV RMSE.
  4. Tune: a larger hyperparameter grid for the selected model.
  5. Evaluate: all models on the holdout set, which is never used for selection or tuning.
# caret method name for each model
benchmark_methods <- c(Random_Forest     = "rf",
                       Gradient_Boosting = "gbm",
                       Elastic_Net       = "glmnet",
                       SVM_Radial        = "svmRadial",
                       KNN               = "knn")

pre_proc <- c("zv", "nzv", "center", "scale")

# Fit one caret model. Without a grid, caret uses its own small default grid.
fit_model <- function(method, X, y, ctrl, grid = NULL) {
  set.seed(42)
  if (method == "gbm") {
    train(x = X, y = y, method = method, trControl = ctrl,
          preProcess = pre_proc, tuneGrid = grid, verbose = FALSE)
  } else {
    train(x = X, y = y, method = method, trControl = ctrl,
          preProcess = pre_proc, tuneGrid = grid)
  }
}

# Larger tuning grid for the winning model (p = number of predictors)
make_grid <- function(model_name, p) {
  if (model_name == "Random_Forest") {
    expand.grid(mtry = unique(c(2, floor(sqrt(p)), floor(p / 3), floor(p / 2), p)))
  } else if (model_name == "Gradient_Boosting") {
    expand.grid(n.trees = c(100, 200, 400), interaction.depth = c(1, 3, 5),
                shrinkage = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1), n.minobsinnode = c(5, 10))
  } else if (model_name == "Elastic_Net") {
    expand.grid(alpha = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
                lambda = 10^seq(-4, 1, length.out = 20))
  } else if (model_name == "SVM_Radial") {
    expand.grid(sigma = c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05),
                C = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20))
  } else {
    expand.grid(k = seq(1, 25, by = 2))
  }
}
run_target <- function(target) {

  # 1. Train / test split
  set.seed(42)
  train_idx <- as.vector(createDataPartition(modeling_data[[target]], p = 0.8, list = FALSE))
  X_train <- modeling_data[train_idx, predictor_cols]
  y_train <- modeling_data[train_idx, target]
  X_test  <- modeling_data[-train_idx, predictor_cols]
  y_test  <- modeling_data[-train_idx, target]

  # 2. The same 5 folds for every model, so the models are directly comparable
  set.seed(42)
  folds <- createFolds(y_train, k = 5, returnTrain = TRUE)
  ctrl  <- trainControl(method = "cv", index = folds, savePredictions = "final")

  # 3. Benchmark models
  models <- list()
  for (name in names(benchmark_methods)) {
    models[[name]] <- fit_model(benchmark_methods[[name]], X_train, y_train, ctrl)
  }

  # 4. Cross-validation table, best model first
  cv_table <- data.frame()
  for (name in names(models)) {
    r <- models[[name]]$resample
    cv_table <- rbind(cv_table, data.frame(
      Model = name, CV_RMSE = mean(r$RMSE), CV_RMSE_SD = sd(r$RMSE),
      CV_R2 = mean(r$Rsquared, na.rm = TRUE), CV_MAE = mean(r$MAE)))
  }
  cv_table  <- cv_table[order(cv_table$CV_RMSE), ]
  best_name <- cv_table$Model[1]

  # 5. Tune the best model
  tuned <- fit_model(benchmark_methods[[best_name]], X_train, y_train, ctrl,
                     grid = make_grid(best_name, ncol(X_train)))

  base_rmse  <- mean(models[[best_name]]$resample$RMSE)
  tuned_rmse <- mean(tuned$resample$RMSE)
  comparison <- data.frame(Model = best_name,
                           Baseline_CV_RMSE = base_rmse,
                           Tuned_CV_RMSE = tuned_rmse,
                           Improvement_pct = 100 * (base_rmse - tuned_rmse) / base_rmse)

  # 6. Holdout evaluation of every model (benchmark + tuned)
  all_models <- models
  all_models[[paste0("Tuned_", best_name)]] <- tuned

  holdout <- data.frame()
  for (name in names(all_models)) {
    pred <- predict(all_models[[name]], newdata = X_test)
    holdout <- rbind(holdout, data.frame(
      Model = name,
      Test_RMSE = rmse(y_test, pred),
      Test_R2 = r2(y_test, pred),
      Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean = 100 * rmse(y_test, pred) / mean(y_test)))
  }

  list(target = target, models = models, cv_table = cv_table,
       best_name = best_name, tuned = tuned, comparison = comparison,
       holdout = holdout, y_test = y_test,
       test_pred = predict(tuned, newdata = X_test))
}

7.1 Diagnostic plot functions

# How stable is each model across the 5 CV folds?
plot_cv_folds <- function(res) {
  fold_df <- data.frame()
  for (name in names(res$models)) {
    fold_df <- rbind(fold_df, data.frame(Model = name, RMSE = res$models[[name]]$resample$RMSE))
  }
  # Best model at the top
  fold_df$Model <- factor(fold_df$Model, levels = rev(res$cv_table$Model))

  ggplot(fold_df, aes(x = RMSE, y = Model, colour = Model, fill = Model)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.45, alpha = 0.18, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.75, position = position_jitter(height = 0.12, seed = 1)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 4.5,
                 colour = "black", stroke = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_cols) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = model_cols) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = pretty_name) +
    labs(title = paste("Model benchmark:", res$target),
         subtitle = "RMSE in each of the 5 CV folds (dots) and the mean (diamond). Lower is better.",
         x = "RMSE", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

# Out-of-fold observed vs predicted, as a 2D density per model
plot_obs_pred <- function(res) {
  oof <- data.frame()
  for (name in names(res$models)) {
    p <- res$models[[name]]$pred
    oof <- rbind(oof, data.frame(Model = pretty_name(name), Observed = p$obs, Predicted = p$pred))
  }
  stats <- oof %>%
    group_by(Model) %>%
    summarise(Label = sprintf("RMSE %.1f\nR² %.2f", rmse(Observed, Predicted), r2(Observed, Predicted)))
  lims <- range(c(oof$Observed, oof$Predicted))

  ggplot(oof, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted)) +
    geom_bin_2d(bins = 28) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = accent, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = forest_dark, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_label(data = stats, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = Label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.15, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold",
               colour = forest_dark, fill = "white") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "G", direction = -1, name = "Plots per cell") +
    coord_equal(xlim = lims, ylim = lims) +
    facet_wrap(~ Model, nrow = 2) +
    labs(title = paste("Observed vs predicted (out-of-fold CV):", res$target),
         subtitle = "Dashed = perfect prediction; solid = fitted trend",
         x = paste("Observed", res$target), y = paste("Predicted", res$target))
}

# Importance scores (0-100) from caret
get_importance <- function(model) {
  imp <- varImp(model, scale = TRUE)$importance
  out <- data.frame(Feature = rownames(imp), Importance = imp[, 1])
  out$Importance[is.na(out$Importance)] <- 0
  out
}

# Heatmap of importance across models + lollipop chart for the tuned model
plot_importance <- function(res, n = 15) {
  imp_all <- data.frame()
  for (name in names(res$models)) {
    imp <- get_importance(res$models[[name]])
    imp$Model <- pretty_name(name)
    imp_all <- rbind(imp_all, imp)
  }
  top <- imp_all %>%
    group_by(Feature) %>%
    summarise(Mean = mean(Importance)) %>%
    arrange(desc(Mean)) %>%
    head(n)

  p_heat <- imp_all %>%
    filter(Feature %in% top$Feature) %>%
    mutate(Feature = factor(Feature, levels = rev(top$Feature))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Model, y = Feature, fill = Importance)) +
    geom_tile(colour = paper, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(Importance), colour = Importance > 60), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#EEF5EC", high = forest_dark, limits = c(0, 100)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey25"), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "Do the models agree?", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

  imp_tuned <- get_importance(res$tuned) %>% arrange(desc(Importance)) %>% head(n)
  p_lolli <- ggplot(imp_tuned, aes(x = Importance, y = reorder(Feature, Importance))) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = Importance, yend = reorder(Feature, Importance)),
                 colour = "grey75", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = Importance), size = 4.5) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "#74C69D", high = forest_dark, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = paste("Tuned", pretty_name(res$best_name)), x = "Importance (0-100)", y = NULL)

  (p_heat | p_lolli) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste("Most important lidar metrics:", res$target),
                    theme = patch_theme)
}

# Tuning profile + fold-by-fold baseline vs tuned
plot_tuning <- function(res) {
  p_profile <- ggplot(res$tuned, highlight = TRUE) +
    labs(title = paste("Tuning profile:", pretty_name(res$best_name))) +
    theme_forest(10)

  base  <- res$models[[res$best_name]]$resample[, c("Resample", "RMSE")]
  tuned <- res$tuned$resample[, c("Resample", "RMSE")]
  folds <- merge(base, tuned, by = "Resample", suffixes = c("_Baseline", "_Tuned"))

  p_folds <- ggplot(folds, aes(y = Resample)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = RMSE_Baseline, xend = RMSE_Tuned, yend = Resample),
                 colour = "grey60", linewidth = 1,
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_point(aes(x = RMSE_Baseline), colour = accent, size = 4) +
    geom_point(aes(x = RMSE_Tuned), colour = forest_dark, size = 4) +
    labs(title = "Baseline → tuned, per fold",
         subtitle = "Orange = baseline, green = tuned",
         x = "RMSE", y = NULL) +
    theme_forest(10)

  (p_profile | p_folds) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(theme = patch_theme)
}

# Final tuned model on the holdout set
plot_holdout <- function(res) {
  d <- data.frame(Observed = res$y_test, Predicted = res$test_pred)
  d$Residual <- d$Observed - d$Predicted
  test_rmse <- rmse(d$Observed, d$Predicted)
  lims <- range(c(d$Observed, d$Predicted))
  res_scale <- scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#3D5A80", mid = "#F4F1DE", high = accent,
                                    midpoint = 0, name = "Residual")

  p_main <- ggplot(d, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = c(-test_rmse, test_rmse),
                colour = "grey60", linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey30", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(fill = Residual), shape = 21, size = 3.2, colour = "white", stroke = 0.4) +
    res_scale +
    coord_equal(xlim = lims, ylim = lims) +
    labs(title = "Observed vs predicted",
         subtitle = sprintf("RMSE = %.2f  |  R² = %.3f  |  dotted lines = ±1 RMSE",
                            test_rmse, r2(d$Observed, d$Predicted)),
         x = paste("Observed", res$target), y = paste("Predicted", res$target)) +
    theme(legend.position = "right")

  p_resid <- ggplot(d, aes(x = Residual)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(fill = after_stat(x)), bins = 20, colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
    res_scale +
    labs(title = "Residuals", x = "Observed − predicted", y = "Plots") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  (p_main | p_resid) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.6, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste("Holdout test set: tuned", pretty_name(res$best_name),
                                  "for", res$target),
                    theme = patch_theme)
}

Training can take several minutes per target (the Gradient Boosting grid is the largest). cache = TRUE means this chunk only re-runs when its code changes.

12 Comparison Across Targets

final_summary <- data.frame()
all_holdout <- data.frame()

for (t in modeling_targets) {
  r <- results[[t]]
  tuned_row <- r$holdout[r$holdout$Model == paste0("Tuned_", r$best_name), ]
  final_summary <- rbind(final_summary, data.frame(
    Target = t, Best_Model = r$best_name,
    CV_RMSE_Baseline = r$comparison$Baseline_CV_RMSE,
    CV_RMSE_Tuned = r$comparison$Tuned_CV_RMSE,
    Test_RMSE = tuned_row$Test_RMSE, Test_R2 = tuned_row$Test_R2,
    Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean = tuned_row$Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean))

  all_holdout <- rbind(all_holdout, cbind(Target = t, r$holdout))
}

kable(final_summary, digits = 3, caption = "Final tuned model per target, evaluated on the holdout set")

all_holdout <- all_holdout %>%
  mutate(Model = ifelse(grepl("^Tuned_", Model), "Tuned best model", pretty_name(Model)),
         Model = factor(Model, levels = c(pretty_name(names(benchmark_methods)), "Tuned best model")))

ggplot(all_holdout, aes(x = Target, y = Model, fill = Test_R2)) +
  geom_tile(colour = paper, linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Test_R2), colour = Test_R2 > 0.5),
            size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "G", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1), name = "Holdout R²") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "Scoreboard: holdout R² for every model and target",
       subtitle = "Darker = better. The bottom row is the tuned version of each target's best model.",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))

ggplot(final_summary, aes(x = Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean,
                          y = reorder(Target, -Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean, yend = reorder(Target, -Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean)),
               colour = "grey75", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 7, colour = forest_dark) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", Test_RMSE_pct_of_mean)),
            colour = "white", size = 2.8, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(label = pretty_name(Best_Model)), hjust = -0.35, colour = "grey35", size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +
  labs(title = "How big is the error compared with a typical plot?",
       subtitle = "Holdout RMSE as a percentage of the target mean (lower is better)",
       x = "RMSE (% of mean)", y = NULL)

13 Conclusions

  • Nha: the best benchmark model was SVM Radial; the tuned model reaches a holdout R² of 0.39 (RMSE = 284.2, 54.9% of the mean).
  • Gha: the best benchmark model was Elastic Net; holdout R² = 0.41 (RMSE = 13.58, 46.4% of the mean).
  • Vol_1v_ha: the best benchmark model was Elastic Net; holdout R² = 0.43 (RMSE = 165.7, 49.5% of the mean).
  • Models were selected and tuned on cross-validation only. The holdout set was used once, for the final evaluation.
  • Other inventory variables were excluded from the predictors, so these results show what the lidar metrics alone can explain.
  • One limitation: the Yeo-Johnson parameters were estimated on the full dataset before the split. Moving this step into caret’s preProcess ("YeoJohnson") would make the holdout test fully independent.
